prompt:
Normalize the single contact record embedded in the user's note. Return only a bare JSON object with exactly the keys "name", "phone", "email", "company", and "country". Each value is a string or JSON null. No other text or Markdown.

Extract only the record's label–value lines. Recognize label variants and shuffled lines, with colon, equals, or tab separators. Never use surrounding notes, signatures, email domains, or legal suffixes to infer missing values. Trim values and collapse whitespace runs to one space. Treat absent lines, blanks, and these whole-value placeholders as missing, case-insensitively: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.

Route values before cleaning them. Reserve the country line for country. Among the other lines, route any value containing @ to email; route a value to phone if, after stripping leading tel: and a trailing numeric extension (ext. N, ext N, xN, #N, extension N), it contains at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, and + - ( ) . /. Do not also use a rerouted value as name or company. Use the remaining labeled name and company values, swapping them if the name-line value ends in a legal suffix and the company-line value does not. Match a trailing suffix case-insensitively as a whole suffix, optionally preceded by a comma: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda.

Resolve phone and country before finalizing any nulls. Map a nonmissing country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 using English, Swedish, or German names, alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes (case-insensitive), and common aliases including UK/Great Britain→GB, Holland→NL, USA/U.S.A.→US, Türkiye→TR, Czech Republic→CZ. Strip tel: and the extension from the phone. If it begins with + or 00 after ignoring an opening parenthesis, it is international: remove (0), remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes, and parentheses, and replace initial 00 with +. Preserve the written calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. With an international phone and a missing country line (including a placeholder), identify the calling code using actual calling-code assignments: if it uniquely identifies a country, you must output that country's alpha-2 code; if it is shared, as with +1 or +7, leave country null. This is the sole exception to missing values staying null. A nonmissing country line always wins. For a national number, remove formatting and exactly one leading trunk 0 if present, then prefix + and the country's calling code; without a country, output phone null. Non-null phones are in E.164 format, a plus followed by digits only.

For name, split at the first comma and reorder Last, First to First Last. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, ignoring case and an optional dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space- or hyphen-separated part. For company, remove the trailing legal suffix and optional preceding comma, trim, then uppercase the first character and lowercase the remainder of each space-separated word. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics through casing; never transliterate. For email, strip surrounding angle brackets and a leading mailto: prefix, including when the prefix is inside or outside the brackets, then lowercase the entire address. Return null for all remaining missing values.
